title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: protect files in excluded Windows folders
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's planned rollout, administrator enablement requirement and minimum client version. The existing exclusion controls and Endpoint DLP licensing are supported; the new control's undocumented configuration is appropriately distinguished from them. One background statement about application storage needs a supporting citation.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Files in excluded Windows paths are outside existing Endpoint DLP enforcement, the gap the planned feature addresses.
claims.quote: Any files that you create or modify in those locations aren't subject to DLP policy enforcement.

claims.claim: The existing exclusion settings documentation says files in excluded locations are not audited.
claims.quote: Files in excluded locations aren't audited.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Learn lists two AppData paths as Windows file paths excluded by default.
claims.quote:
Windows file paths excluded by default

- `%SystemDrive%\\Users\\*(1)\\AppData\\Roaming`
- `%SystemDrive%\\Users\\*(1)\\AppData\\Local`

claims.claim: Applications write data in application-data and temporary folders.
claims.quote: The folders where your app can store data. These folders (local, roaming and temporary) are created when your app is installed.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/apps/develop/files/file-access-permissions to sources to support the application-storage premise in 'Users and applications write to AppData and temporary folders'.

claims.claim: Existing Windows file path exclusions are configured in Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Overview > Data loss prevention settings > Endpoint settings > File path exclusions for Windows.
claims.quote: go to [Microsoft Purview portal](https://purview.microsoft.com) > **Data loss prevention** > **Overview** > **Data loss prevention settings** > **Endpoint settings** > **File path exclusions for Windows**.

claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig -EndpointDlpGlobalSettings @(@{"Setting"="PathExclusion"; "Value"="<path>"}) configures an existing endpoint path exclusion.
claims.quote:
The EndpointDlpGlobalSettings parameter specifies the global endpoints. ... Example values:

- `@{"Setting"="PathExclusion"; "Value"="C:\Windows";}`
- `@{"Setting"="PathExclusion"; "Value"="%AppData%\Mozilla";}`

claims.claim: Set-PolicyConfig is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: The existing endpoint file path exclusion settings are tenant-wide settings applying to all DLP policies for devices.
claims.quote: Centrally configured settings control many aspects of endpoint data loss prevention (DLP) behavior. These settings apply to all DLP policies for devices.

claims.claim: No admin UI path or automation call is yet documented for enabling the new protection for files in excluded Windows folders.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP excluded folders protect settings; Set-PolicyConfig protected exclusion. Opened Configure endpoint data loss prevention settings and Set-PolicyConfig; both document existing exclusions, not the new protection switch.

claims.claim: The configuration scope of the new protection is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP protected exclusion roles scope. Read MC1384420, Configure endpoint data loss prevention settings and Set-PolicyConfig; none specifies whether the new protection switch is tenant-wide, per policy or per path.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published which admin roles can configure the new excluded-folder protection setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP protected exclusion roles scope; Endpoint DLP excluded folders identity permissions. Read MC1384420, endpoint settings and Set-PolicyConfig; no role is assigned to this new, undocumented setting.

claims.claim: The available sources describe no identity or permission change for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Endpoint DLP excluded folders identity permissions. Read the roadmap record, full MC1384420 and endpoint settings documentation; none describes an identity or permission change for excluded-folder protection.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Existing per-user Endpoint DLP licensing covers Windows endpoint protections, so the change is classified as included in the product's existing licensing.
claims.quote: The per-user licensing model is the familiar Microsoft 365 E3/E5/A5/F5/G5 model. It remains unchanged. This licensing model enables you to apply Microsoft Purview controls and protections to Microsoft 365 and Windows/macOS endpoint-based assets.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP is included in Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW, Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW, and Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection & Governance.
claims.quote:
| Feature | Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW and Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW, Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection & Governance |
| --- | --- |
| Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) | Included |
